description: Classify a bounded positive integer by the Lucas–Carmichael criterion.

source.title: Lucas-Carmichael numbers
source.discovery_scope: RosettaCodeData is title discovery only. The definition comes from OEIS A006972 and MathWorld; no task wording, source code, examples, or tests are copied.

output.meaning: 1 iff n is squarefree composite and every prime p dividing n satisfies (p+1) divides (n+1); 0 otherwise

contract.criterion: Lucas-Carmichael numbers are squarefree composite n such that for each prime divisor p of n, p+1 divides n+1.
contract.small_values: The accepted value 1, primes, and all composites failing the criterion return 0.
contract.primary_factor_bound: For n<=1000000, residual trial division tests integer candidates from 2 through at most floor(sqrt(n))<=1000, at most 999 candidates. Each discovered prime factor must have exponent one.
contract.independent_reference_bound: A sieve through 1000 supplies 168 primes; the reference checks each possible divisor against the original n, detects repeated factors using p^2, then checks the remaining cofactor.
contract.arithmetic: All native arithmetic is signed 64-bit; n+1 and every divisor+1 are at most 1000001.

workspace.meaning: Conservative native scalar scratch allowance for factor, divisor, exponent, and loop state; caller-owned input is excluded.

complexity.independent_reference_time: O(B log log B + pi(B)) after a bounded sieve, B=1000

suite_status: integrated in i64_array_scalar runner and verifier
